title: Water Damage Mitigation Estimating Guideline for Mitigation Service Lines
content:
This Water Damage Mitigation estimating guideline governs mitigation service and labor lines: extraction, treatment, tear-out, protection, contents, debris, labor and inspection work booked on a job.

## Clauses in force
- The job must be in authorized, drying or drying complete status when a mitigation service line is charged.
- Moisture mapping and thermal imaging are billed at most once per job.
- Antimicrobial is billed only on tiers where antimicrobial treatment is required, and PPE only on tiers where PPE is billable.
- Carpet that may be salvaged on the job's tier is billed as detach and reset, and carpet that may not be salvaged is billed as carpet removal; carpet detach and reset and carpet removal are mutually exclusive for the same area.
- Carpet pad is billed as pad removal only on tiers where pad salvage is not allowed.
- Technician and supervisor labor performed in the after-hours or holiday window is billed at the hourly rate times the after-hours labor multiplier, and that adjusted rate is the line's unit rate.
- Amounts are rounded to the cent, half up.

## Retired clause
The following clause of this guideline is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for billing mitigation service lines and is kept here as a record only:

> Each mitigation service is billed at the unit rate of the job's tier for its service code, multiplied by the quantity performed: extraction, antimicrobial, pad and carpet work and HEPA vacuuming by the square foot, flood cuts and baseboard by the linear foot, contents manipulation by the room, debris by the load, PPE by the technician-day, labor by the hour, and moisture mapping, thermal imaging, containment, dumpster, lead-safe setup and asbestos sampling by the each.

## Carpet and pad decision table
| The job's tier allows | Wet carpet is billed as | Wet carpet pad |
|---|---|---|
| carpet salvage | carpet detach and reset | billed as pad removal only where pad salvage is not allowed |
| no carpet salvage | carpet removal | billed as pad removal only where pad salvage is not allowed |

For one and the same area, a job never carries both a carpet detach and reset line and a carpet removal line.

## Labor in the after-hours or holiday window (hypothetical)
With an assumed hourly rate of $70.00 and a multiplier of 1.5, an after-hours technician line carries a unit rate of $105.00, and that adjusted rate is what the line shows as its unit rate.
